title: Anticholinergic burden at hospital discharge and injurious falls in adults aged 70 and over
subtitle: Design not yet settled: cohort or case-control
statement: Older adults are often discharged from the medical wards on several medicines with anticholinergic effects, and the pharmacy team scores this burden inconsistently. It is not known locally whether a high anticholinergic burden at discharge is followed by more injurious falls within 90 days once frailty and the reasons for prescribing are taken into account. The answer decides whether pharmacist deprescribing review before discharge should become routine for everyone aged 70 or over.
whoAffected: Adults aged 70 and over discharged from the medical wards, their families and carers, the clinical pharmacy team whose time is at stake, and the geriatric medicine consultants who asked the question.
whatHurts: Injurious falls after discharge cause fractures, head injuries, readmission and loss of independence. Pharmacist time spent scoring burden without knowing whether it predicts harm is time not spent on reviews that might prevent it.
currentPractice: Anticholinergic burden is scored for some patients at discharge with a drug-weighting score (0 to 3 points per drug), with no threshold that triggers action and no follow-up of outcomes.
whyNow: Consultants are asking for routine deprescribing review for all older adults, which would take substantial pharmacist time, and the dispensing and regional admission data needed to answer the question already exist.
patientCenteredGoal: Older adults go home on the fewest medicines that could make them fall, without losing the benefit of the medicines they need.
summary: Problem framed; the design family is left unresolved (cohort or case-control) until the evidence and the data are reviewed.
